questions.q: Consider the following reaction, and choose the correct option.
options: Compound $\text{P}$ is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on BaSO$_4$.
On treating compound $\text{P}$ with saturated NaHCO$_3$ solution, brisk effervescence is observed.
Compound $\text{P}$ can be prepared by treating benzene with anhydrous AlCl$_3$ and CH$_3$COCl.
On treatment with bromine water, compound $\text{P}$ gives a white precipitate.
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the Etard reaction. Toluene reacts with chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in a non-polar solvent like $\text{CS}_2$ to form a chromium complex, which upon acid hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) yields benzaldehyde.

Therefore, compound $\text{P}$ is benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

Let us evaluate the given options:

Option (1): The hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Pd supported on $\text{BaSO}_4$ is known as the Rosenmund reduction. This reaction yields benzaldehyde. Thus, this statement is correct.

Option (2): Benzaldehyde does not react with saturated $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solution to give brisk effervescence. This test is characteristic of carboxylic acids.

Option (3): Treating benzene with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) is a Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction, which produces acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$), not benzaldehyde.

Option (4): Benzaldehyde does not give a white precipitate with bromine water. The bromine water test giving a white precipitate is characteristic of phenol and aniline.

Answer: Compound $\text{P}$ is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on BaSO$_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I:
trans-But-2-ene upon treatment with Br$_2$ in CCl$_4$ gives the following product

Statement II:
cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline KMnO$_4$ gives the following product

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution:
Reaction of trans-but-2-ene with Br$_2$ in CCl$_4$ proceeds via anti-addition to give meso-2,3-dibromobutane.

In the Newman projection given in Statement I, the front carbon has Br at $0^{\circ}$, Me at $120^{\circ}$, and H at $240^{\circ}$. The back carbon has Br at $180^{\circ}$, Me at $60^{\circ}$, and H at $300^{\circ}$. For this staggered conformation to be meso, it must have a center of inversion, meaning a group at angle $\theta$ on the front carbon must have an identical group at $\theta + 180^{\circ}$ on the back carbon. While the Br atoms are opposite ($0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$), the front Me at $120^{\circ}$ is not opposite to the back Me at $60^{\circ}$. Thus, it lacks a center of inversion and represents a chiral enantiomer. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.

Reaction of cis-but-2-ene with alkaline KMnO$_4$ proceeds via syn-addition to give meso-butane-2,3-diol.

In the Newman projection given in Statement II, the front carbon has OH at $0^{\circ}$, Me at $120^{\circ}$, and H at $240^{\circ}$. The back carbon has OH at $60^{\circ}$, Me at $180^{\circ}$, and H at $300^{\circ}$. Rotating the back carbon by $60^{\circ}$ counter-clockwise perfectly eclipses all identical groups (OH with OH at $0^{\circ}$, Me with Me at $120^{\circ}$, H with H at $240^{\circ}$). This indicates the presence of a plane of symmetry, confirming it is the meso isomer. Hence, Statement II is correct.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.q: Among the following, the compound having conjugated double bonds is
questions.solution:
Conjugated double bonds are separated by exactly one single bond.

In hepta-1,6-diene, the double bonds are at C1 and C6, separated by three single bonds.

In hepta-1,3-diene, the double bonds are at C1 and C3, separated by exactly one single bond (between C2 and C3). Thus, it has conjugated double bonds.

In hepta-1,4-diene, the double bonds are at C1 and C4, separated by two single bonds.

In hepta-1,5-diene, the double bonds are at C1 and C5, separated by three single bonds.

Answer: hepta-1,3-diene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option
options: If $\text{P}$ is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, $\text{Q}$ is a primary alcohol.
If $\text{P}$ gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, $\text{Q}$ gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.
questions.solution:
The first step is the Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, which produces acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$).

The second step is the haloform reaction. Acetophenone has a methyl ketone group and reacts with sodium hypochlorite ($\text{NaOCl}$) to form sodium benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$) and chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$).

Thus, the products $\text{P}$ and $\text{Q}$ are sodium benzoate and chloroform.

Sodium benzoate ($\text{P}$) on acidification yields benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$).

Chloroform ($\text{Q}$) on exposure to air and light oxidizes to form phosgene ($\text{COCl}_2$), a highly poisonous gas, according to the reaction:
$2\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{light}} 2\text{COCl}_2 + 2\text{HCl}$

Therefore, if $\text{P}$ gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, $\text{Q}$ gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.

Answer: If $\text{P}$ gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, $\text{Q}$ gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two products X and Y are formed in the following reaction sequence.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} W \xrightarrow[\text{warm}]{\text{dil. HNO}_3 + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} X + Y$
The suitable method that can be used for the separation of products X and Y is :
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with methyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation, which yields toluene (W).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3$

Nitration of toluene with a mixture of $\text{HNO}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields a mixture of ortho-nitrotoluene and para-nitrotoluene as the major products (X and Y).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{warm}]{\text{dil. HNO}_3 + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{o-nitrotoluene} + \text{p-nitrotoluene}$

The boiling point of o-nitrotoluene is $222^\circ\text{C}$ and that of p-nitrotoluene is $238^\circ\text{C}$. Since the difference in their boiling points is small, they are separated by fractional distillation.

Answer: Fractional distillation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are :
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} X$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} Y$
questions.solution:
Reaction 1 is an electrophilic aromatic substitution. Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (a Lewis acid) to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6 + 6\text{HCl}$

The organic product X is hexachlorobenzene, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Reaction 2 is a free radical addition reaction. Benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of UV light to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), also known as gammaxene or lindane.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$

The organic product Y is benzene hexachloride, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Therefore, the number of chlorine atoms in both X and Y is $6$.

Answer: $6$ and $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the following reaction sequences and choose the correct option.
questions.solution:
The given starting material is 1-phenylpropyne, $\text{Ph}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{Me}$.

Reduction of the alkyne with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Lindlar's catalyst ($\text{Pd/C}$ poisoned with $\text{BaSO}_4$ or quinoline) proceeds via syn-addition. This yields the cis-alkene. Therefore, $\text{K}$ is cis-1-phenylpropene.

Reduction of the alkyne with $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ (Birch reduction conditions) proceeds via anti-addition. This yields the trans-alkene. Therefore, $\text{L}$ is trans-1-phenylpropene.

Since $\text{K}$ is the cis-isomer and $\text{L}$ is the trans-isomer of the same compound, they are geometrical isomers.

Further reactions:
Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to $\text{K}$ is an electrophilic addition that proceeds via the more stable benzylic carbocation ($\text{Ph}-\text{C}^+\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Me}$). This gives 1-bromo-1-phenylpropane as product $\text{M}$.

Addition of $\text{HBr}$ to $\text{L}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide is a free radical addition (anti-Markovnikov). The bromine radical adds to form the more stable benzylic radical ($\text{Ph}-\text{C}^\bullet\text{H}-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{Me}$). This gives 2-bromo-1-phenylpropane as product $\text{N}$.

$\text{M}$ and $\text{N}$ are positional isomers (constitutional isomers), not stereoisomers.

Thus, the only correct statement is that $\text{K}$ and $\text{L}$ are geometrical isomers.

Answer: $\text{K}$ and $\text{L}$ are geometrical isomers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The order of decreasing reactivity towards an electrophilic reagent, for the following would be:
(i) benzene
(ii) toluene
(iii) chlorobenzene 
(iv) phenol
questions.solution:
Electrophiles have high affinity for electrons. They attack at the site where electron-density is highest. Electron withdrawing substances increases the electron density. The electron withdrawing tendency decreases in the order :
$-\mathrm{OH}>-\mathrm{CH}_3>-\mathrm{H}>-\mathrm{Cl}$
Therefore, the correct order of reactivity towards electrophile is
$\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}>\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}_3>\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6>\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Cl}$
Related Theory
Electrophilic substitution reaction in haloarenes occur slowly because halogen has a negative inductive effect, it decreases the electron density on the benzene ring due to resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of reactivity towards the electrophillic substitution of the compounds aniline (I), benzene (II) and nitrobenzene (III) is:
questions.solution:
Nitro group $\left(-\mathrm{NO}_2\right)$ is an electron withdrawing group. It removes electron density from aromatic nucleus. Thus, the reactivity of nitrobenzene towards electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction is less. Amine group $\left(-\mathrm{NH}_2\right)$ is an electron releasing group. They increase the electron density on benzene ring. Thus, aniline is more reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substituion reaction than benzene.
Hence, the correct order of reactivity towards the electrophilic substitution of the compounds is.
aniline $(\mathrm{I})>$ benzene (II) $>$ nitrobenzene (III).

Reason $(\mathrm{R})$ : Addition of $\mathrm{HBr}$ to unsymmetrical alkenes proceeds according to Markovnikov's rule
The correct answer is
options: (A) and (R) are correct, (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): "Reaction of 1-butene with HBr gives 1-bromobutane as a major product." This is incorrect. According to Markovnikov's rule, the hydrogen atom of HBr adds to the carbon atom of the double bond that already has more hydrogen atoms. Thus, in the reaction of 1butene (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2\)) with HBr, the hydrogen adds to \(\mathrm{CH}_2\) and the bromine adds to the second carbon atom (\(C H\)) to give 2-bromobutane as the major product.
- Reason (R): "Addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes proceeds according to Markovnikov's rule." This is correct. Markovnikov's rule states that for an electrophilic addition reaction of a protic acid (like HBr) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the proton adds to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms, and the halide adds to the more substituted carbon.
The assertion is incorrect, but the reason is correct. Therefore, the answer is (4) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

A. A is more soluble than $B$.
B. The boiling point & melting point of $A$are higher and lower than $B$ respectively.

C. A is more polar than $B$ because dipole moment of $A$ is zero.
D. ${Br}_{2}$ adds easily to $B$ than $A$.
questions.solution:

B: Trans - But-2-ene

More polar molecules are more soluble in ${H}_{2}O$. Hence A >B.

Molecules having higher dipole moments have higher boiling points due to larger intermolecular forces of attraction. More symmetric isomers have higher melting points due to better packing in crystalline lattice & trans isomers are more symmetric than cis. Hence, in case of boiling point it is A>B and in case of melting point it is B>A.

cis-isomer has resultant of dipoles while in trans isomer dipole moments cancel out. 

So, the correct answer is B, C and D only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 2,2-Dimethylpropane is readily oxidized to an alcohol by alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.
Reason (R): Alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom are oxidized to corresponding alcohols by potassium permanganate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false. 2,2-Dimethylpropane (neopentane) has the structure $\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$. The central carbon is quaternary ($4^{\circ}$) and is bonded to four methyl groups. It does not possess any tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) hydrogen atom. Therefore, it resists oxidation by alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Reason (R) is true. As a general rule, alkanes are inert towards oxidizing agents. However, as an exception, alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom can be oxidized to the corresponding tertiary alcohol by potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$).

Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form an aromatic compound, whereas with chlorine in the presence of UV light it forms a non-aromatic compound.
Reason (R): Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ generates chlorine free radicals which undergo substitution, whereas UV light generates electrophiles which undergo addition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: Benzene reacts with excess $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (dark, cold) to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$), which retains the aromatic ring. However, benzene reacts with $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of UV light to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), which is a saturated, non-aromatic compound.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The roles of the reactive intermediates are swapped in the statement. Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is a Lewis acid that generates the chloronium ion ($\text{Cl}^+$), which is an electrophile, leading to electrophilic aromatic substitution. Conversely, UV light causes homolytic cleavage of the $\text{Cl}-\text{Cl}$ bond to generate chlorine free radicals ($\text{Cl}^\bullet$), which lead to free radical addition.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Photochemical monochlorination of 2,2-dimethylbutane yields exactly four structurally isomeric products.

Reason (R): The molecule of 2,2-dimethylbutane possesses three distinct sets of equivalent hydrogen atoms: nine primary hydrogens, two secondary hydrogens, and three other primary hydrogens.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The structure of 2,2-dimethylbutane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

Let us identify the sets of equivalent hydrogen atoms in the molecule:
First, the three methyl groups attached to C-2 are equivalent, providing a set of 9 primary hydrogens.
Second, the methylene group at C-3 provides a set of 2 secondary hydrogens.
Third, the terminal methyl group at C-4 provides a set of 3 primary hydrogens.

Since there are exactly three distinct sets of equivalent hydrogen atoms, the photochemical monochlorination of 2,2-dimethylbutane will yield exactly three structurally isomeric products (1-chloro-2,2-dimethylbutane, 3-chloro-2,2-dimethylbutane, and 1-chloro-3,3-dimethylbutane).

Therefore, Assertion (A) is incorrect because it claims four products are formed, while Reason (R) is correct as it accurately describes the three sets of equivalent hydrogens.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following two reactions:
(i) $\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{A}$ (major monochloro product)
(ii) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu,\ 500\ \text{K}} \text{B}$

The types of reaction mechanisms involved in the formation of A and B, respectively, are :
options: Free radical substitution and Free radical addition
Free radical substitution and Free radical substitution
Electrophilic substitution and Free radical addition
Free radical addition and Electrophilic substitution
questions.solution:
Reaction (i) is the halogenation of an alkane (methane) in the presence of sunlight or UV light ($h\nu$). This proceeds via a free radical substitution mechanism to form chloromethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$).

Reaction (ii) is the reaction of benzene with chlorine in the presence of UV light at 500 K. Under these conditions, the stable aromatic ring undergoes a free radical addition reaction to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), completely saturating the ring.

Therefore, the mechanisms are free radical substitution and free radical addition, respectively. Students often incorrectly assume that UV light will cause substitution in benzene just as it does in alkanes, but the addition pathway is followed instead.

Answer: Free radical substitution and Free radical addition

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

$2$-Bromopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH, }\Delta}$ A (Major product)

A $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) Zn/H}_{2}\text{O}]{\text{(i) O}_{3}}$ B + C

Identify the IUPAC names of the final products B and C.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Reaction of $2$-bromopentane with alcoholic KOH undergoes $\beta$-elimination (dehydrohalogenation). According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is the major product. Thus, the major product A is pent-$2$-ene.

Step 2: Reductive ozonolysis of pent-$2$-ene (CH$_{3}$-CH=CH-CH$_{2}$-CH$_{3}$) cleaves the double bond to form two aldehyde molecules.

CH$_{3}$-CH=CH-CH$_{2}$-CH$_{3}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{O}_{3}, \text{ Zn/H}_{2}\text{O}}$ CH$_{3}$CHO + CH$_{3}$CH$_{2}$CHO

Hence, the products B and C are Ethanal and Propanal.

Methanal and Butanal would be formed from the minor product (pent-$1$-ene). Ethanoic acid and Propanoic acid would be formed if oxidative ozonolysis was performed.

Answer: Ethanal and Propanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene yields propanone and ethanal as the products. The IUPAC name of the alkene is
questions.solution:
The products of reductive ozonolysis are propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) and ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

To find the structure of the original alkene, remove the oxygen atoms from the carbonyl groups and join the corresponding carbon atoms with a double bond.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$

Numbering the longest carbon chain to give the double bond the lowest possible number, we get 2-methylbut-2-ene.

2-Methylbut-1-ene yields butan-2-one and methanal.
3-Methylbut-1-ene yields 2-methylpropanal and methanal.
Pent-2-ene yields ethanal and propanal.

Answer: 2-Methylbut-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A brown chromium complex is formed as an intermediate when a hydrocarbon 'X' is treated with a reagent 'Y'. The hydrolysis of this complex yields an aldehyde 'Z' which reduces Tollens' reagent but does not reduce Fehling's solution. Identify 'X' and 'Y'.
questions.solution:
Aldehyde 'Z' reduces Tollens' reagent but not Fehling's solution, which is a characteristic property of aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde.

The formation of a brown chromium complex intermediate during the oxidation of a hydrocarbon to benzaldehyde is the hallmark of the Etard reaction.

In the Etard reaction, toluene (hydrocarbon 'X') is treated with chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in a non-polar solvent like $\text{CS}_2$ (reagent 'Y') to form the brown chromium complex, which on subsequent acid hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.

Using $\text{CrO}_3$ in acetic anhydride would yield benzylidene diacetate as the intermediate, not a chromium complex.

Answer: X = Toluene, Y = $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the reactions of toluene.

List-I (Reagents)List-II (Intermediate / Product)
(A) $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2, \text{CS}_2$(I) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OCrOHCl}_2)_2$
(B) $\text{CrO}_3, (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$(II) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OCOCH}_3)_2$
(C) $\text{Cl}_2, h\nu$(III) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHCl}_2$
(D) $\text{KMnO}_4, \text{KOH}, \Delta$(IV) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}^-\text{K}^+$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{CS}_2$ to form a brown chromium complex intermediate, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OCrOHCl}_2)_2$. This is the Etard reaction. Thus, (A) matches with (I).

Toluene reacts with chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$) in acetic anhydride to form benzylidene diacetate, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OCOCH}_3)_2$. Thus, (B) matches with (II).

Side chain chlorination of toluene with $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of sunlight gives benzal chloride, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHCl}_2$. Thus, (C) matches with (III).

Strong oxidation of toluene with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ upon heating yields potassium benzoate, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}^-\text{K}^+$, which on acidification gives benzoic acid. Thus, (D) matches with (IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.q:
Consider the following alkanes:
(i) Propane
(ii) Isobutane
(iii) Neopentane
(iv) 2-Methylbutane
(v) $n$-Pentane
(vi) 3-Ethylpentane

How many of the above alkanes can be oxidized to the corresponding alcohol by alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$?
questions.solution:
Alkanes are generally inert to oxidation. However, alkanes containing a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) hydrogen atom can be oxidized to the corresponding alcohol by strong oxidizing agents like alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Let us examine the given alkanes for the presence of a $3^{\circ}$ hydrogen atom:
(i) Propane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_3}$): Contains only $1^{\circ}$ and $2^{\circ}$ hydrogens.
(ii) Isobutane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_3}$): Contains one $3^{\circ}$ hydrogen.
(iii) Neopentane ($\mathrm{C(CH_3)_4}$): Contains only $1^{\circ}$ hydrogens attached to a quaternary carbon.
(iv) 2-Methylbutane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3}$): Contains one $3^{\circ}$ hydrogen.
(v) $n$-Pentane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3}$): Contains only $1^{\circ}$ and $2^{\circ}$ hydrogens.
(vi) 3-Ethylpentane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH(C_2H_5)CH_2CH_3}$): Contains one $3^{\circ}$ hydrogen.

Thus, Isobutane, 2-Methylbutane, and 3-Ethylpentane can be oxidized by $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$. The total number of such alkanes is 3.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene is treated with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to yield compound $\text{P}$. Which of the following statements is correct regarding compound $\text{P}$?
options: It reduces Tollens' reagent to give a silver mirror.
It produces a yellow precipitate when warmed with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide.
It can be prepared by the vigorous oxidation of ethylbenzene with alkaline potassium permanganate.
It reacts with bromine water to form a white precipitate.
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is a Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction. The product $\text{P}$ formed is acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$).

Let us evaluate the given options:

Option (1): Acetophenone is a ketone and does not reduce Tollens' reagent. This test is characteristic of aldehydes.

Option (2): Acetophenone is a methyl ketone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$). It undergoes the iodoform reaction when warmed with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide to give a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$). Thus, this statement is correct.

Option (3): The vigorous oxidation of ethylbenzene with alkaline potassium permanganate yields benzoic acid, not acetophenone.

Option (4): Acetophenone does not give a white precipitate with bromine water. This test is characteristic of phenol and aniline.

Answer: It produces a yellow precipitate when warmed with iodine and aqueous sodium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many structurally isomeric monochloro products are obtained upon the photochemical chlorination of isopentane?
questions.solution:
The structure of isopentane is 2-methylbutane, $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3}$.

To find the number of structurally isomeric monochloro products, we identify the number of non-equivalent sets of hydrogen atoms.

In isopentane, there are four different types of hydrogen atoms:
(i) The primary hydrogens of the two equivalent methyl groups attached to C-2.
(ii) The tertiary hydrogen at C-2.
(iii) The secondary hydrogens at C-3.
(iv) The primary hydrogens of the methyl group at C-4.

Since there are 4 sets of non-equivalent hydrogens, photochemical chlorination yields exactly 4 structurally isomeric monochloro products.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reactions of benzene:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} X$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} Y$

Which of the following statements correctly describes the structural properties of products $X$ and $Y$?
options: Both $X$ and $Y$ are aromatic compounds containing only $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atoms.
$X$ is an aromatic compound with $sp^2$ hybridized carbons, while $Y$ is a non-aromatic compound with $sp^3$ hybridized carbons.
Both $X$ and $Y$ are non-aromatic compounds containing only $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms.
$X$ is a non-aromatic compound with $sp^3$ hybridized carbons, while $Y$ is an aromatic compound with $sp^2$ hybridized carbons.
questions.solution:
Reaction 1 is a free radical addition reaction. Benzene reacts with $3$ molecules of chlorine in the presence of UV light to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), which is product $X$. In this addition reaction, the aromatic $\pi$-electron cloud is destroyed, and all carbon atoms become $sp^3$ hybridized. Thus, $X$ is non-aromatic.

Reaction 2 is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction. Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$), which is product $Y$. In this substitution reaction, the hydrogen atoms are replaced by chlorine atoms, but the aromatic ring remains intact. All carbon atoms in $Y$ remain $sp^2$ hybridized. Thus, $Y$ is aromatic.

Therefore, $X$ is a non-aromatic compound with $sp^3$ hybridized carbons, and $Y$ is an aromatic compound with $sp^2$ hybridized carbons.

Answer: $X$ is a non-aromatic compound with $sp^3$ hybridized carbons, while $Y$ is an aromatic compound with $sp^2$ hybridized carbons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unknown alkene 'X' undergoes two different reaction sequences:
Sequence 1: 'X' is treated with $\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6$ followed by $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2/\mathrm{OH}^-$, and the resulting product is oxidized with Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) to give compound 'Y'. Compound 'Y' gives a positive Tollens' test but a negative iodoform test.
Sequence 2: 'X' is subjected to acid-catalyzed hydration, and the resulting product is oxidized with $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ to give compound 'Z'. Compound 'Z' gives a positive iodoform test but a negative Tollens' test.

Identify the alkene 'X'.
questions.solution:
For Sequence 1, hydroboration-oxidation followed by PCC yields an aldehyde 'Y' (since it gives a positive Tollens' test). This indicates that 'X' must be a terminal alkene, and 'Y' cannot be ethanal (as ethanal gives a positive iodoform test).

For Sequence 2, acid-catalyzed hydration followed by $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ oxidation yields a methyl ketone 'Z' (since it gives a positive iodoform test but a negative Tollens' test).

Let us evaluate the given options:
1) Ethene: Sequence 1 yields ethanal, which gives a positive iodoform test (violating the condition for 'Y').
2) But-2-ene: Sequence 1 yields butan-2-one, which gives a negative Tollens' test (violating the condition for 'Y').
3) Propene: Sequence 1 yields propan-1-ol, which on PCC oxidation gives propanal ('Y'). Propanal gives a positive Tollens' test and a negative iodoform test. Sequence 2 yields propan-2-ol, which on $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ oxidation gives propanone ('Z'). Propanone gives a positive iodoform test and a negative Tollens' test. This matches all conditions.
4) 2-Methylpropene: Sequence 2 yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol (a tertiary alcohol), which resists oxidation by $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ and does not form a methyl ketone.

Thus, the alkene 'X' is propene.

Answer: Propene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When $2$-bromo-$2$-methylbutane is heated with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, a major alkene is formed. Identify the IUPAC name of this major product and the rule that governs its formation.
questions.solution:
The reaction of $2$-bromo-$2$-methylbutane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ is a dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination) reaction.

The structure of $2$-bromo-$2$-methylbutane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$. It has two different types of $\beta$-hydrogens.

Elimination of a proton from the terminal $\text{CH}_3$ group yields $2$-methylbut-$1$-ene (a disubstituted alkene).

Elimination of a proton from the internal $\text{CH}_2$ group yields $2$-methylbut-$2$-ene (a trisubstituted alkene).

According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is more stable and is formed as the major product. Therefore, $2$-methylbut-$2$-ene is the major product.

Answer: $2$-Methylbut-$2$-ene and Zaitsev rule

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkanes can be readily oxidized to an alcohol by potassium permanganate ($\mathrm{KMnO}_4$)?
questions.solution:
Generally, alkanes are inert towards strong oxidizing agents such as $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$. However, alkanes containing a tertiary hydrogen atom are an exception and can be oxidized to the corresponding tertiary alcohols.

Let us examine the structures of the given alkanes:
1) 2-Methylbutane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$. The carbon at position 2 is a tertiary carbon, so it possesses a tertiary hydrogen atom.
2) $n$-Butane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$. It contains only primary and secondary hydrogen atoms.
3) 2,2-Dimethylpropane: $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_4$. It contains a quaternary carbon and primary hydrogen atoms, but no tertiary hydrogen.
4) $n$-Hexane: $\mathrm{CH}_3-(\mathrm{CH}_2)_4-\mathrm{CH}_3$. It contains only primary and secondary hydrogen atoms.

Thus, only 2-Methylbutane will be oxidized by $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ to form 2-Methylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: 2-Methylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the presence of peroxide, addition of HBr to but-1-ene yields 2-bromobutane as the major product, while addition of HI yields 1-iodobutane.
Reason (R): The H-I bond is weaker than the H-Br bond, causing iodine free radicals to combine to form iodine molecules instead of adding to the double bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The Assertion (A) is false. The addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes like but-1-ene in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov's rule, yielding 1-bromobutane as the major product. However, the peroxide effect is not observed with HI. The addition of HI always follows Markovnikov's rule, even in the presence of peroxide, yielding 2-iodobutane.

The Reason (R) is true. The peroxide effect fails for HI because the H-I bond is relatively weak. As a result, the iodine free radicals generated during the reaction readily combine with each other to form iodine molecules ($\text{I}_2$) instead of adding to the double bond of the alkene.

Therefore, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

Therefore, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following alkyl bromides:
(A) 3-Bromocyclohexene
(B) Bromocyclohexane
(C) 1-Bromohexane

The correct decreasing order of their reactivity towards dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH is:
questions.solution:
The rate of dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination) is directly proportional to the stability of the major alkene formed.

(A) 3-Bromocyclohexene undergoes dehydrohalogenation to form cyclohexa-1,3-diene, which is highly stable due to conjugation.

(B) Bromocyclohexane undergoes dehydrohalogenation to form cyclohexene, which is stabilized by hyperconjugation (it is a disubstituted alkene).

(C) 1-Bromohexane undergoes dehydrohalogenation to form hex-1-ene, which is a monosubstituted terminal alkene and is the least stable among the three.

Since conjugated dienes are more stable than isolated disubstituted alkenes, which in turn are more stable than monosubstituted alkenes, the stability order of the products is cyclohexa-1,3-diene > cyclohexene > hex-1-ene.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is (A) > (B) > (C).

Answer: (A) > (B) > (C)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the preparation of aldehydes and ketones:
I. Stephen reaction involves the reduction of nitriles with $\text{SnCl}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ followed by hydrolysis to give aldehydes.
II. Etard reaction involves the oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde using chromyl chloride.
III. Treatment of acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium yields aldehydes.
IV. Hydration of propyne in the presence of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ gives propanal.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. Nitriles are reduced to the corresponding imine with stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid, which on hydrolysis gives the corresponding aldehyde (Stephen reaction).

Statement II is correct. Chromyl chloride oxidises the methyl group of toluene to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde (Etard reaction).

Statement III is incorrect. Treatment of acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium yields ketones, not aldehydes.

Statement IV is incorrect. Hydration of propyne in the presence of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{HgSO}_4$ follows Markovnikov's addition to give propanone (a ketone), not propanal.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic compound 'X' reacts with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to give a yellow precipitate and the sodium salt of an acid 'Y'. Acid 'Y' on heating with soda lime produces benzene. Compound 'X' can be synthesized by the reaction of benzene with reagent 'Z' in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$. Identify compound 'X' and reagent 'Z'.
options: 'X' is Benzaldehyde and 'Z' is Formyl chloride
'X' is Acetophenone and 'Z' is Acetyl chloride
'X' is Propiophenone and 'Z' is Propanoyl chloride
'X' is Toluene and 'Z' is Methyl chloride
questions.solution:
Acid 'Y' undergoes decarboxylation on heating with soda lime ($\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CaO}$) to produce benzene, which indicates that 'Y' is benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$).

The sodium salt of 'Y' is sodium benzoate. Compound 'X' reacts with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium benzoate and a yellow precipitate (iodoform, $\text{CHI}_3$). This positive iodoform test indicates that 'X' is a methyl ketone, specifically acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$).

Acetophenone ('X') is synthesized by the Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene using acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) as reagent 'Z' in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$.

Thus, 'X' is acetophenone and 'Z' is acetyl chloride.

Answer: 'X' is Acetophenone and 'Z' is Acetyl chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II for the products obtained upon reductive ozonolysis ($O_3/Zn, H_2O$) of the given alkenes.

(A)2-Methylpropene(I)Propanone and Ethanal
(B)But-2-ene(II)Propanone and Methanal
(C)Cyclopentene(III)Pentanedial
(D)2-Methylbut-2-ene(IV)Ethanal only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of alkenes cleaves the C=C double bond to form carbonyl compounds.

(A) 2-Methylpropene ($(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$) has a terminal double bond and yields propanone and methanal.
(B) But-2-ene ($CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3$) is a symmetrical internal alkene and yields two moles of ethanal.
(C) Cyclopentene is a cyclic alkene. Cleavage of the ring yields a single molecule with two aldehyde groups, pentanedial ($OHC-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CHO$).
(D) 2-Methylbut-2-ene ($(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_3$) has an internal double bond with one branched carbon, yielding propanone and ethanal.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reaction of $2$-bromobutane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ yields but-$2$-ene as the major product.

Reason (R): In $\beta$-elimination reactions, the preferred product is that alkene which has the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: When $2$-bromobutane is heated with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, dehydrohalogenation occurs. It can form but-$1$-ene and but-$2$-ene. But-$2$-ene is the major product.

Reason (R) is correct: Zaitsev's rule states that in dehydrohalogenation reactions, the preferred product is that alkene which has the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms.

Since but-$2$-ene is a disubstituted alkene and but-$1$-ene is a monosubstituted alkene, Zaitsev's rule explains why but-$2$-ene is the major product. Thus, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Transformation of but-1-ene to butanal can be achieved using $\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6$ followed by $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2/\mathrm{OH}^-$ and subsequently reacting the product with Pyridinium Chlorochromate (PCC).

Reason (R): Hydroboration-oxidation of but-1-ene yields butan-1-ol via anti-Markovnikov addition of water, and primary alcohols are selectively oxidized to aldehydes by PCC.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The Assertion is true: the sequence of hydroboration-oxidation ($\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6$ followed by $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2/\mathrm{OH}^-$) converts a terminal alkene (but-1-ene) to a primary alcohol (butan-1-ol). Subsequent oxidation with a mild oxidizing agent like PCC converts the primary alcohol to an aldehyde (butanal) without over-oxidizing it to a carboxylic acid.

The Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion: the regioselectivity of hydroboration-oxidation follows anti-Markovnikov addition, placing the hydroxyl group on the less substituted carbon to form butan-1-ol, which is essential for forming the aldehyde upon oxidation with PCC.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

List-I (Reactions of Benzene)List-II (Major Product)
(A) With $3\text{Cl}_2$ in presence of UV light at $500\ \text{K}$(I) Hexachlorobenzene
(B) With excess $\text{Cl}_2$ in presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in dark(II) Benzene hexachloride
(C) With $3\text{H}_2$ in presence of Ni at high temperature and pressure(III) Cyclohexane
(D) With $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ in presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$(IV) Toluene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of UV light to undergo free radical addition, forming benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$). So, (A) matches with (II).

(B) Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (a Lewis acid) in the dark to undergo electrophilic substitution, forming hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$). So, (B) matches with (I).

(C) Benzene undergoes catalytic hydrogenation with $3\text{H}_2$ in the presence of finely divided nickel at high temperature and pressure to form cyclohexane. So, (C) matches with (III).

(D) Benzene reacts with methyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to form toluene. So, (D) matches with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The heavy organic liquid obtained by the reaction of acetophenone with sodium hypochlorite produces a foul-smelling compound when heated with aniline and ethanolic potassium hydroxide.
Reason (R): Acetophenone undergoes the haloform reaction with sodium hypochlorite to form chloroform, which then gives a positive carbylamine test with primary amines.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$) contains a methyl ketone group. When treated with sodium hypochlorite ($\text{NaOCl}$), it undergoes the haloform reaction to yield sodium benzoate and chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$).

Chloroform is a heavy organic liquid. When chloroform is heated with a primary amine such as aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) and ethanolic potassium hydroxide, it undergoes the carbylamine reaction.

The product of the carbylamine reaction is phenyl isocyanide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NC}$), which is characterized by a highly offensive or foul smell.

Therefore, the heavy organic liquid is chloroform, and it produces a foul-smelling isocyanide upon reaction with aniline and ethanolic $\text{KOH}$.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true statements, and Reason (R) provides the correct chemical explanation for the observation described in Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Assertion (A): In the preparation of benzaldehyde from toluene using chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$), acetic anhydride is used to prevent further oxidation of benzaldehyde to benzoic acid.

Reason (R): The intermediate formed, benzylidene diacetate, is resistant to further oxidation and is subsequently hydrolysed to benzaldehyde.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The use of chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$) in acetic anhydride converts toluene to benzylidene diacetate.

This diacetate intermediate is stable and does not undergo further oxidation to benzoic acid, effectively trapping the oxidation at the aldehyde stage.

It is then isolated and hydrolysed with aqueous acid to yield the final product, benzaldehyde.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains why acetic anhydride is used to prevent over-oxidation.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the preparation of benzaldehyde from toluene using chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$), acetic anhydride is used to prevent further oxidation of benzaldehyde to benzoic acid.

Reason (R): The intermediate formed, benzylidene diacetate, is resistant to further oxidation and is subsequently hydrolysed to benzaldehyde.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
The use of chromic oxide ($\text{CrO}_3$) in acetic anhydride converts toluene to benzylidene diacetate.

This diacetate intermediate is stable and does not undergo further oxidation to benzoic acid, effectively trapping the oxidation at the aldehyde stage.

It is then isolated and hydrolysed with aqueous acid to yield the final product, benzaldehyde.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains why acetic anhydride is used to prevent over-oxidation.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reactions that produce alkyl halides as their major products:
(I) Addition of HBr to 2-methylbut-2-ene
(II) Addition of HBr to but-1-ene
(III) Addition of HBr to ethene

The correct increasing order of the rate of dehydrohalogenation of these resulting major alkyl halides with alcoholic KOH is:
questions.solution:
According to Markovnikov's rule, the addition of HBr to the given alkenes yields the following major alkyl halides:

(I) 2-Methylbut-2-ene + HBr $\rightarrow$ 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane (a $3^{\circ}$ alkyl halide)
(II) But-1-ene + HBr $\rightarrow$ 2-Bromobutane (a $2^{\circ}$ alkyl halide)
(III) Ethene + HBr $\rightarrow$ Bromoethane (a $1^{\circ}$ alkyl halide)

The rate of dehydrohalogenation (E2 reaction) with alcoholic KOH depends on the stability of the transition state and the resulting alkene. Tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) alkyl halides form more highly substituted, stable alkenes and react the fastest, while primary ($1^{\circ}$) alkyl halides react the slowest.

Thus, the increasing order of the rate of dehydrohalogenation is $1^{\circ} < 2^{\circ} < 3^{\circ}$, which corresponds to (III) $<$ (II) $<$ (I).

Answer: (III) $<$ (II) $<$ (I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:
$\text{2-Methylprop-1-ene} \xrightarrow[\text{Peroxide}]{\text{HBr}} \text{X} \xrightarrow[\text{Dry ether}]{\text{Na}} \text{Y}$
The IUPAC name of the major product Y is:
questions.solution:
Step 1: 2-Methylprop-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$) reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide to undergo anti-Markovnikov addition. The bromine atom adds to the less substituted carbon, yielding 1-bromo-2-methylpropane as intermediate X.

Step 2: 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane (X) undergoes the Wurtz reaction when treated with sodium in dry ether. Two molecules of the alkyl halide couple together to form an alkane.

$2 \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{NaBr}$

The longest carbon chain has 6 carbon atoms with methyl groups at the 2nd and 5th positions. Thus, the IUPAC name of product Y is 2,5-dimethylhexane.

If Markovnikov addition had occurred (due to the absence of peroxide), the intermediate would be 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, which would lead to 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

Answer: 2,5-Dimethylhexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aromatic compound 'A' with the molecular formula $\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$ on reduction with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ gives compound 'B'. Compound 'B' upon treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at $273-278\text{ K}$ followed by warming with water gives compound 'C'. Compound 'C' reacts with bromine water to form a tribromo derivative. Identify compound 'A'.
questions.solution:
Compound 'A' ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{NO}_2$) is a nitrotoluene.

Reduction of nitrotoluene with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ yields a toluidine ('B').

Diazotization of toluidine followed by hydrolysis (warming with water) yields a cresol ('C').

For a cresol to form a tribromo derivative upon reaction with bromine water, all three positions ortho and para to the activating $-\text{OH}$ group must be unsubstituted.

In $m$-cresol (3-methylphenol), the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is at the meta position, leaving both ortho positions and the para position free for electrophilic aromatic substitution. Thus, it forms 2,4,6-tribromo-3-methylphenol.

In contrast, $o$-cresol and $p$-cresol have one of these positions blocked by the methyl group and can only form dibromo derivatives.

Therefore, 'C' is $m$-cresol, 'B' is $m$-toluidine, and 'A' is $m$-nitrotoluene.

Answer: $m$-Nitrotoluene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product formed when pent-1-ene is treated with HCl in the presence of benzoyl peroxide?
questions.solution:
The peroxide effect (anti-Markovnikov addition) is observed only with HBr. It is not observed with HCl or HI because one of the steps in their free radical mechanism is endothermic.

Therefore, even in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, the addition of HCl to pent-1-ene follows Markovnikov's rule via an electrophilic addition mechanism.

The proton ($\text{H}^{+}$) adds to the terminal carbon to form the more stable secondary carbocation. The chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) then attacks this carbocation to form 2-chloropentane as the major product.

Answer: 2-Chloropentane

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Mixtures)List-II (Separation Methods)
(A) Mixture of $o$-nitrotoluene and $p$-nitrotoluene(I) Fractional distillation
(B) Mixture of $o$-dichlorobenzene and $p$-dichlorobenzene(II) Fractional crystallization
(C) Mixture of chloroform and aniline(III) Simple distillation
(D) Mixture of aniline and water(IV) Steam distillation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) The mixture of $o$-nitrotoluene and $p$-nitrotoluene contains isomers with a small difference in boiling points and no hydrogen bonding. They are separated by fractional distillation.

(B) The mixture of $o$-dichlorobenzene and $p$-dichlorobenzene is separated by fractional crystallization because the para-isomer has a much higher melting point due to its symmetrical structure.

(C) Chloroform (bp ~334 K) and aniline (bp ~457 K) have a large difference in their boiling points and are separated by simple distillation.

(D) Aniline is steam volatile and immiscible with water, so a mixture of aniline and water is separated by steam distillation.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl halide $\text{X}$ undergoes Wurtz reaction to yield an alkane $\text{Y}$ with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$. Alkane $\text{Y}$, upon photochemical monochlorination, yields exactly two structural isomers. Identify the starting alkyl halide $\text{X}$.
questions.solution:
The alkane $\text{Y}$ has the formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$. Since it yields exactly two structural isomers upon monochlorination, it must possess exactly two distinct sets of equivalent hydrogen atoms.

Let us evaluate the possible symmetrical hexanes formed via Wurtz reaction:
First, $n$-hexane (from 1-chloropropane) has three sets of equivalent hydrogens, yielding 3 monochloro isomers.
Second, 2,3-dimethylbutane (from 2-chloropropane) has 12 equivalent primary hydrogens and 2 equivalent tertiary hydrogens. It yields exactly 2 monochloro isomers.

Thus, alkane $\text{Y}$ is 2,3-dimethylbutane.

In the Wurtz reaction, two identical alkyl radicals couple to form the alkane. To obtain 2,3-dimethylbutane, the reacting alkyl halide must be an isopropyl halide.
Therefore, the starting alkyl halide $\text{X}$ is 2-chloropropane.

(Note: Chloroethane yields $n$-butane, which gives 2 isomers but has the formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$, not $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$. 1-Chloro-2-methylpropane yields 2,5-dimethylhexane, which gives 3 isomers.)

Answer: 2-Chloropropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The isomeric mixture obtained by the electrophilic nitration of toluene is separated by steam distillation.
Reason (R): $o$-Nitrotoluene is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.solution:
Electrophilic nitration of toluene yields a mixture of $o$-nitrotoluene and $p$-nitrotoluene. Unlike $o$-nitrophenol, $o$-nitrotoluene does not possess intramolecular hydrogen bonding because the hydrogen atoms of the methyl group do not participate in hydrogen bonding with the nitro group.

Since there is no significant difference in volatility caused by hydrogen bonding, and their boiling points are relatively close, the mixture of $o$-nitrotoluene and $p$-nitrotoluene is separated by fractional distillation, not steam distillation.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are incorrect statements.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are not correct

Match List I with List II.

List I (Reaction Sequence)List II (Major Product)
A. Aniline $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Br}_2\text{(aq)}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273 K}} \xrightarrow{\text{(iii) H}_3\text{PO}_2}$I. 1,3,5-Tribromobenzene
B. Aniline $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Ac}_2\text{O, pyridine}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) Br}_2\text{/CH}_3\text{COOH}} \xrightarrow{\text{(iii) H}_3\text{O}^+} \xrightarrow{\text{(iv) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273 K}} \xrightarrow{\text{(v) H}_3\text{PO}_2}$II. Bromobenzene
C. $p$-Toluidine $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273 K}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) CuCN}}$III. 4-Methylbenzonitrile
D. $p$-Nitroaniline $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273 K}} \xrightarrow{\text{(ii) HBF}_4\text{, }\Delta}$IV. 1-Fluoro-4-nitrobenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A. Aniline reacts with bromine water to form 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Diazotization followed by reduction with $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ replaces the diazonium group with hydrogen, yielding 1,3,5-tribromobenzene. (A $\rightarrow$ I)

B. Protection of aniline with acetic anhydride yields acetanilide, which on bromination gives $p$-bromoacetanilide as the major product. Hydrolysis yields $p$-bromoaniline. Diazotization and subsequent reduction with $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ removes the amino group, yielding bromobenzene. (B $\rightarrow$ II)

C. $p$-Toluidine is diazotized and treated with $\text{CuCN}$ (Sandmeyer reaction) to replace the diazonium group with a cyanide group, yielding 4-methylbenzonitrile. (C $\rightarrow$ III)

D. $p$-Nitroaniline is diazotized and treated with fluoroboric acid ($\text{HBF}_4$) followed by heating (Balz-Schiemann reaction) to yield 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene. (D $\rightarrow$ IV)

Answer: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene reacts with propene in the presence of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ to form compound A. Oxidation of A by $\text{O}_2$ followed by acidic hydrolysis yields an aromatic compound B and an aliphatic compound C. When compound C is treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, what is the identity of C and the visible observation in this final step?
options: C is propanal; a silver mirror is formed
C is acetic acid; brisk effervescence occurs
C is acetone; a yellow precipitate is formed
C is ethanol; a yellow precipitate is formed
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with propene in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$) is an alkylation reaction that yields cumene (isopropylbenzene) as compound A.

Cumene (A) undergoes air oxidation to form cumene hydroperoxide, which on subsequent acidic hydrolysis yields phenol (aromatic compound B) and acetone (aliphatic compound C, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$).

Acetone (C) contains a methyl ketone group ($\text{-COCH}_3$) and therefore gives a positive iodoform test. When treated with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$, it undergoes the haloform reaction to produce a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) and sodium acetate.

Thus, compound C is acetone and a yellow precipitate is formed.

Answer: C is acetone; a yellow precipitate is formed

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound 'X' forms a 2,4-DNP derivative and reduces Tollens' reagent, but does not reduce Fehling's solution. Which of the following combinations of starting material and reagent(s) can be used to prepare compound 'X'?
options: Benzene and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$
Toluene and alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by heating and acidification
Benzene and $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{FeCl}_3$
questions.solution:
The formation of a 2,4-DNP derivative indicates that compound 'X' is a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone).

Since 'X' reduces Tollens' reagent but does not reduce Fehling's solution, it must be an aromatic aldehyde, such as benzaldehyde. Aliphatic aldehydes reduce both Tollens' and Fehling's reagents, while ketones reduce neither.

Let us evaluate the given preparation methods:
Option (1): Toluene reacts with chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{CS}_2$ followed by acid hydrolysis to give benzaldehyde (Etard reaction). This matches the properties of compound 'X'.

Option (2): Benzene reacts with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to give acetophenone (a ketone), which does not reduce Tollens' reagent.

Option (3): Toluene is oxidised by alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ to benzoic acid, which does not form a 2,4-DNP derivative.

Option (4): Benzene reacts with $\text{Cl}_2$/$\text{FeCl}_3$ to give chlorobenzene, which is not a carbonyl compound.

Answer: Toluene and $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ in $\text{CS}_2$ followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$

Assertion (A): 1-Chloro-1-phenylbutane undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH at a faster rate than 3-chloro-1-phenylbutane.
Reason (R): 3-Chloro-1-phenylbutane contains more number of $\beta$-hydrogen atoms than 1-chloro-1-phenylbutane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: The rate of dehydrohalogenation (E2 reaction) depends on the thermodynamic stability of the product alkene. 1-Chloro-1-phenylbutane yields 1-phenylbut-1-ene, where the newly formed double bond is in conjugation with the benzene ring, providing high stability. 3-Chloro-1-phenylbutane yields 1-phenylbut-2-ene, where the double bond is isolated from the benzene ring. Thus, 1-chloro-1-phenylbutane reacts at a faster rate.

Reason (R) is correct: 3-Chloro-1-phenylbutane ($C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH_3$) has 5 $\beta$-hydrogen atoms (two on C2 and three on C4). 1-Chloro-1-phenylbutane ($C_6H_5-CH(Cl)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$) has only 2 $\beta$-hydrogen atoms (on C2).

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The correct explanation is the thermodynamic stability of the conjugated alkene product, not the number of $\beta$-hydrogen atoms.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene is treated with propanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to yield compound $\text{P}$. Compound $\text{P}$ is then warmed with an alkaline solution of iodine. What is the expected outcome of the second step?
options: A yellow precipitate of iodoform is formed along with sodium benzoate.
A yellow precipitate of iodoform is formed along with sodium phenylacetate.
Electrophilic substitution occurs on the aromatic ring to yield an iodinated product.
No yellow precipitate is formed because $\text{P}$ lacks a methyl group adjacent to the carbonyl carbon.
questions.solution:
The first step is a Friedel-Crafts acylation. Benzene reacts with propanoyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form propiophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$), which is compound $\text{P}$.

The second step involves warming compound $\text{P}$ with an alkaline solution of iodine ($\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$), which is the reagent for the haloform (iodoform) test.

The iodoform test is positive only for compounds containing a methyl ketone group ($\text{-COCH}_3$) or a secondary alcohol group oxidizable to a methyl ketone ($\text{-CH(OH)CH}_3$).

Propiophenone is an ethyl ketone; it has a $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group attached to the carbonyl carbon, not a $\text{-CH}_3$ group. Therefore, it cannot form the triiodo intermediate required for cleavage.

As a result, the haloform reaction fails, and no yellow precipitate of iodoform is formed.

Answer: No yellow precipitate is formed because $\text{P}$ lacks a methyl group adjacent to the carbonyl carbon.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) But-1-ene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6 \text{ (ii) } \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2/\mathrm{OH}^-} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}}$(I) Butan-2-one
(B) But-1-ene $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{H}^+} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{CrO}_3}$(II) Ethanal
(C) But-1-ene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6 \text{ (ii) } \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2/\mathrm{OH}^-} \xrightarrow{\text{(i) alk. } \mathrm{KMnO}_4 \text{ (ii) } \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+}$(III) Butanal
(D) But-2-ene $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) } \mathrm{O}_3 \text{ (ii) } \mathrm{Zn}/\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}}$(IV) Butanoic acid


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Hydroboration-oxidation of but-1-ene yields butan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov addition of water). Oxidation of butan-1-ol with PCC (a mild oxidizing agent) yields butanal. Thus, (A) matches with (III).

(B) Acid-catalyzed hydration of but-1-ene yields butan-2-ol (Markovnikov addition). Oxidation of butan-2-ol with $\mathrm{CrO}_3$ yields butan-2-one. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

(C) Hydroboration-oxidation of but-1-ene yields butan-1-ol. Oxidation with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ (a strong oxidizing agent) followed by acidification yields butanoic acid. Thus, (C) matches with (IV).

(D) Reductive ozonolysis of but-2-ene cleaves the double bond to yield two molecules of ethanal. Thus, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A chemical reaction produces a mixture of two isomers. These isomers have a small difference in their boiling points, do not exhibit hydrogen bonding, and are typically separated by fractional distillation.

Which of the following reactions yields a product mixture that best matches these characteristics?
options: Chlorination of chlorobenzene with $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{FeCl}_3$
Nitration of toluene with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
Alkylation of benzene with chloromethane in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$
questions.solution:
Nitration of toluene yields a mixture of $o$-nitrotoluene and $p$-nitrotoluene. These isomers do not exhibit hydrogen bonding and have a small difference in their boiling points, making fractional distillation the suitable separation method.

Nitration of phenol yields $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol, which exhibit intramolecular and intermolecular hydrogen bonding respectively, and are separated by steam distillation.

Chlorination of chlorobenzene yields $o$-dichlorobenzene and $p$-dichlorobenzene, which are separated by fractional crystallization due to a large difference in their melting points.

Alkylation of benzene with chloromethane yields toluene as the single major product, not a mixture of isomers.

Answer: Nitration of toluene with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl bromide X with the molecular formula $C_5H_{11}Br$ exhibits the highest rate of dehydrohalogenation among all its structural isomers. When treated with alcoholic KOH, X undergoes elimination to majorly form an alkene Y. Ozonolysis of Y followed by treatment with $Zn/H_2O$ yields a mixture of propan-2-one and ethanal. The IUPAC name of the alkyl bromide X is:
questions.solution:
The reductive ozonolysis of alkene Y yields propan-2-one ($CH_3COCH_3$) and ethanal ($CH_3CHO$). Working backwards, the structure of alkene Y must be 2-methylbut-2-ene ($CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$).

The alkyl bromide X ($C_5H_{11}Br$) that yields 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product upon dehydrohalogenation could be either 2-bromo-2-methylbutane (a $3^{\circ}$ halide) or 2-bromo-3-methylbutane (a $2^{\circ}$ halide).

The problem states that X exhibits the highest rate of dehydrohalogenation among its structural isomers. Since tertiary alkyl halides undergo E2 elimination faster than secondary and primary halides due to the formation of a more stable transition state and a more substituted alkene, X must be the tertiary halide, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

Answer: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason.

Assertion: Reductive ozonolysis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene yields octane-2,7-dione.
Reason: Reductive ozonolysis of any substituted cycloalkene always yields a diketone.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct: 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene has a double bond between two methyl-bearing carbons in a six-membered ring. Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the ring at the double bond, converting C1 and C2 into ketone groups. The resulting structure is $CH_3-C(=O)-(CH_2)_4-C(=O)-CH_3$, which is an eight-carbon chain with ketones at positions 2 and 7, named octane-2,7-dione.

Reason is incorrect: Reductive ozonolysis of a substituted cycloalkene does not always yield a diketone. It depends on the substitution pattern at the double bond. For example, ozonolysis of 1-methylcyclohexene (which has only one alkyl substituent on the double bond) yields 7-oxoheptanal, which is a keto-aldehyde, not a diketone.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene reacts with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminum chloride and cuprous chloride to form compound $\text{X}$. When compound $\text{X}$ is heated with concentrated sodium hydroxide, it yields two compounds, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$. The compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) and hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{CuCl}$ is the Gattermann-Koch reaction. The product $\text{X}$ formed is benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

Benzaldehyde does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When heated with a concentrated alkali like concentrated $\text{NaOH}$, aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo the Cannizzaro reaction. This is a disproportionation reaction where one molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol and another is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

Therefore, benzaldehyde disproportionates to yield benzyl alcohol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) and sodium benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$).

Thus, compounds $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ are sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

Option (1) is incorrect because it assumes $\text{X}$ is phenol. Option (2) is incorrect because it assumes a simple acid-base neutralization or complete oxidation. Option (4) is incorrect because sodium formate would be a product of a cross-Cannizzaro reaction with formaldehyde.

Answer: Sodium benzoate and benzyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product $X$ formed in the following reaction sequence:

2-Nitroanisole $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) Sn/HCl}]{\text{(i) Br}_2\text{/FeBr}_3}$ $\text{Intermediate} \xrightarrow[\text{(iv) H}_3\text{PO}_2\text{/H}_2\text{O}]{\text{(iii) NaNO}_2\text{/HCl, 273 K}} X$
questions.solution:
In 2-nitroanisole, the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is strongly activating and ortho/para directing, while the $-\text{NO}_2$ group is deactivating and meta directing. Both groups synergistically direct the incoming electrophile ($\text{Br}^+$) to the position para to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group (position 4) as it is less sterically hindered than the ortho position. This yields 4-bromo-2-nitroanisole.

Treatment with $\text{Sn/HCl}$ reduces the $-\text{NO}_2$ group to an $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming 4-bromo-2-methoxyaniline.

Reaction with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at 273 K converts the amine into a diazonium salt.

Finally, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2\text{/H}_2\text{O}$ reduces the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom (deamination), yielding 4-bromoanisole as the final major product $X$.

Answer: 4-Bromoanisole

D. The removal of a hydrogen atom from the $\beta$-carbon (the carbon adjacent to the one carrying the halogen) is known as $\beta$-elimination (D-IV).

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

3-phenylprop-1-ene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{OH}^-]{\text{(i) } \mathrm{BH}_3\cdot\mathrm{THF}}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{PCC}}$ B

The major product 'B' is:
questions.solution:
Hydroboration-oxidation of 3-phenylprop-1-ene proceeds via anti-Markovnikov addition of water to the double bond, yielding a primary alcohol, 3-phenylpropan-1-ol (Product A). The presence of the phenyl ring does not alter the regioselectivity of this concerted mechanism.

Subsequent oxidation of this primary alcohol with Pyridinium Chlorochromate (PCC), a mild oxidizing agent, selectively yields an aldehyde without over-oxidizing it to a carboxylic acid. Thus, the final product B is 3-phenylpropanal.

Answer: 3-phenylpropanal

questions.solution:
The starting material, $p$-toluidine (4-methylaniline), is first treated with acetic anhydride ($\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$) in pyridine to protect the highly reactive $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming $N$-acetyl-$p$-toluidine.

During bromination ($\text{Br}_2\text{/CH}_3\text{COOH}$), the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group is a stronger activating and directing group than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group. Thus, the incoming electrophile ($\text{Br}^+$) is directed to the position ortho to the $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$ group, yielding 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide.

Acid hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) removes the acetyl protecting group to give 2-bromo-4-methylaniline.

Treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at 273 K converts the primary amine into a diazonium salt.

Finally, reaction with $\text{CuCN}$ (Sandmeyer reaction) replaces the diazonium group with a nitrile ($-\text{CN}$) group, resulting in 2-bromo-4-methylbenzonitrile.

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

Toluene $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } \text{H}_3\text{O}^+]{\text{(i) } \text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2, \text{CS}_2} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{273-283 K}]{\text{Conc. } \text{HNO}_3 + \text{Conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{B}$

The major product 'B' is:
questions.solution:
Step 1 is the Etard reaction. Toluene is oxidised by chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{CS}_2$ followed by acid hydrolysis to give benzaldehyde (Compound A).

Step 2 is the nitration of benzaldehyde. The aldehydic group ($-\text{CHO}$) is an electron-withdrawing group and acts as a meta-directing, deactivating group in electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Therefore, nitration of benzaldehyde with a nitrating mixture (concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) yields $m$-nitrobenzaldehyde as the major product (Compound B).

Students who assume the $-\text{CHO}$ group is ortho/para directing will incorrectly choose $o$- or $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde. Students who ignore the reaction sequence and nitrate toluene directly will incorrectly choose $p$-nitrotoluene.

Answer: $m$-Nitrobenzaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkene with the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ yields only a single type of carbonyl compound upon reductive ozonolysis. If the alkene also exhibits geometrical isomerism, its IUPAC name is
questions.solution:
The alkene yields only a single type of carbonyl compound upon reductive ozonolysis, which indicates that it must be a symmetrical alkene. For the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$, the possible symmetrical acyclic alkenes are hex-3-ene and 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene. Cyclohexene is a cyclic alkene that also yields a single product (hexanedial) upon ozonolysis.

The question states that the alkene exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism. For geometrical isomerism to occur, each carbon atom of the double bond must be attached to two different groups.

In 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, each double-bonded carbon is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.
Cyclohexene does not exhibit geometrical isomerism because the trans-isomer is highly strained and does not exist under normal conditions.
Hex-2-ene shows geometrical isomerism but yields two different products (ethanal and butanal) on ozonolysis.
Hex-3-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is symmetrical (yielding only propanal on ozonolysis) and each double-bonded carbon is attached to a hydrogen atom and an ethyl group, allowing it to exhibit geometrical isomerism.

Therefore, the alkene is hex-3-ene.

Answer: Hex-3-ene

questions.q: Which of the following reactions will yield 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane as the major product?
options: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the absence of peroxide
2,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HCl in the presence of peroxide
questions.solution:
The target product is 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane, which is a primary alkyl bromide.

To obtain a primary alkyl bromide from a terminal alkene without altering the carbon skeleton, anti-Markovnikov addition is required. This is achieved by the reaction of the alkene with HBr in the presence of a peroxide (Kharasch effect).

The starting alkene must have the same carbon skeleton. Thus, 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene reacting with HBr and peroxide will yield 1-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane.

In the absence of peroxide, HBr would undergo Markovnikov addition with a methyl shift, yielding 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane. HCl does not exhibit the peroxide effect and would follow Markovnikov's rule.

Answer: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene + HBr in the presence of peroxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rate determining step in nitration of benzene is
questions.solution:
The nitration of benzene takes places in three steps, i.e.
(i) Generation of electrophile $\left(\mathrm{NO}_2^{+}\right)$
(ii) Attack of an electrophile to benzene ring forming the carbocation
(iii) Loss of proton from carbocation giving nitrobenzene.
The attack of electrophile to benzene ring giving a carbocation is the slowest and rate determining step.

questions.q: $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ for the reaction, $\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{s}) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Ag}(s)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{~g})$, are $30.56 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $66.00 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The temperature at which the free energy change for the reaction will be zero, is
questions.solution:
From the Gibb's - Helmholtz equation,
$\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S$
At equilibrium, $\Delta G=0$
Hence, $\quad \Delta H-T \Delta S=0$ or, $\Delta H=T \Delta S$
Or,$T=\frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$
Given that, $\Delta H=30.56 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \begin{aligned} & =30560 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ \therefore \quad \Delta S & =66.0 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ \therefore \quad T & =\frac{30560}{66.0}=463 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The homologue of ethyne is
questions.solution: Ethyne is nothing but $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2$ ie, acetylene which can be represented by general molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_n \mathrm{H}_{2 n-2}$. Only $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_4$ tallies with the formula. Hence, $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_4$ is the homologue of $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Butyne-1 and butyne- 2 can be distinguished by
questions.solution:
Butyne-1 has the terminal hydrogen atom which reacts with ammonical silver nitrate easily and liberate hydrogen.
$2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{CH}+\mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \underset{\text{white ppt}}{\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{CAg}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}}$
Hence butyne- 1 and butyne- 2 are distinguished by $\mathrm{AgNO}_3+\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is 'X' in the following sequence?
Ar. $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{Cl} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{KCN}]{$$\mathrm{CuCN}$$} $$\mathrm{Z}$$ \xrightarrow{$$\mathrm{H}$$. $$\mathrm{OH}$$} $$\mathrm{Y}$ \xrightarrow[\Delta]{$\text{ soda-lime }$ } $\mathrm{X}$
questions.solution:
The reaction sequence is as follows:
\(\mathrm{ArN}_2 \mathrm{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{ Sandmeyer's reaction }]{\mathrm{CuCNKCN}}\mathrm{ArCN} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H} . \mathrm{OH}} \underset{\text{benzoic acid}}{\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COOH}}\xrightarrow[\text{ decarboxylation }]{\Delta \text{, sodalime }} \underset{\text{ benzene }}{\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6}\)
